question.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}+2\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3{x}^{2}+2){e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2}+2)(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})-\int (\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(3{x}^{2}+2){e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{6}{3}\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(3{x}^{2}+2){e}^{3x}}{3}-2\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})-\int (\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}+D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(3x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3{x}^{2}+2){e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(3{x}^{2}+2){e}^{3x}}{3}-2(\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(3x-1)+D) \\  & =\frac{(3{x}^{2}+2){e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{2{e}^{3x}}{9}(3x-1)-2D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(3(3{x}^{2}+2)-2(3x-1))-2D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3x}}{9}(9{x}^{2}-6x+8)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$
